# Report: video15, L1 proxy, Three.js sampled-frame baseline

Representation level: L1 (proxy). This is the CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline. It is not equivalent to the Blender protocol.

Observed in the 24 reference samples: a single continuous helmet-camera point-of-view shot of a downhill ski run in heavy fog, lasting 15 s at 30 fps. The broadcast captions read Mausefalle, Karussellkurve and Steilhang. The scene has:
- white snow with blue dye lines
- white A1 advertising boards, and red Generali and dark Hahnenkamm banners along the course edges
- red/orange safety netting
- snow-covered conifers and spectators
- teal distance signs and a lattice tower
- orange gates with a black label
- the rider's red ski tips, which appear at the bottom of the frame in some samples

Geometry: the course is a procedural snow ribbon built along a precomputed centreline, using heading, slope, bank and side-hill tables. Fences are instanced boxes, and the netting uses translucent boxes. Trees are instanced cones. Gates are cylinders plus a box panel. Signs, the tower and the spectators are boxes and cylinders. Broadcast overlays (captions and logo) are not reproduced, because they are not scene content.

Camera and timing: the camera rides the centreline at a constant 26 m/s, about 1.15 m above the snow. It follows the path heading and the local slope, plus keyframed yaw, pitch and roll offsets and a lateral offset fitted at each sample time. The ski tips are two red boxes attached to the camera. Their image position and visibility are keyframed from the samples. I modelled the clip as one shot with no cuts.

Inference: the course geometry between samples, the speed, and the exact turn radii are inferred. The section layout comes from fence sides and horizon slants in the samples.

Feedback: none received yet. This is the initial round.

rounds.reason: Fix fog, pitch, bank/roll, fence placement and ski tips after round 1 comparison

- The left side is open at the crest.
- The Karussell traverse has a steeper side hill and bank.
- Roll is retuned in the Karussell.
- Trees are wider and darker.

Round 5 brings the left Steilhang fence closer by the end of the clip and lightens the trees slightly.

Submission: the round 5 render is submitted. In the side-by-side pairs it matches the references on these points:
- course direction, fence sides and colours
- the gate passages at about 3.3 s, 7.2 s and 12.4 s
- the cross-slope and roll in the Karussell traverse
- the left turn after the crest, followed by the close left-side Generali fence in the Steilhang
- the visibility of the ski tips at the bottom of the frame

Remaining discrepancies:
- The trees are pale geometric cones, not snow-laden conifers.
- Banner text, broadcast captions and the logo are not reproduced.
- Several horizon slants are approximated with camera roll rather than true terrain shape, so the trees do not stay perfectly vertical.
- In some frames the right-side hill and the fence distances differ from the reference.
- Speed is held constant, and the geometry between samples is inferred.
